description_en: In the Newar settlements of the Kathmandu Valley, it is customary forŚāktaimages to be housed within adyaḥchẽ—a shrine for lineage deities (dyaḥ)—rather than in independent temples. TheViṣṇudevīshrine atMacchegāũstands as a striking exception to this tradition. Here, a three-tiered temple structure has been erected by incorporating thedyahchẽitself into the architectural design.Macchegāũ is a small Newar settlement where, as in other Newar villages, a guardian goddess (kṣetrapāla)—one among theŚāktagoddesses—is mandatorily enshrined; in this case, the presiding deity isViṣṇudevī. Although the structure outwardly appears as a typical three-tieredpagoda-style temple, its function and ritual significance align with that of adyahchẽ. The tangible image installed on the first floor of the shrine represents the intangible goddess believed to reside outside the settlement—a tradition common to many Newar communities. Accordingly, at Macchegāũ, the anthropomorphic image ofViṣṇudevīoccupies the first floor rather than the ground level.The main deity,Viṣṇudevī, is accompanied by otherŚāktadeities such asBhairava,Gaṇeśa,Cāmuṇḍā (Kālikā), andMāheśvarī. The originalmukhākṛtis (metallic face-plaques) of these deities were stolen during the c. 1960s CE (VS 2020s), and the present ones are replicas; only the face ofGaṇeśaremains an original piece. The building that houses these images was originally a rectangular, east–west oriented two-storeyeddyahchẽṃ. The addition of twophucā(attic) tiers later transformed it into a three-storeyedpagoda-style temple.At the temple’s frontage stand two stone lions dated to 1720 CE (NS 790), flanking a richly ornamented wooden doorway surmounted by atoraṇa. The presenttoraṇais a modern replica, replacing the original that was stolen during the 1990s CE (VS 2050s). Two ritual flags are placed on either side of the entrance. In earlier times, all three roofs were covered with traditional clay tiles (jhigāṭī), but during post-earthquake restoration works, these were replaced by copper sheets.No inscription precisely dating the temple’s construction has yet been discovered. The earliest known inscription from the site dates to 1670 CE (NS 790), recording the dedication of a pair of lion statues in honor of Viṣṇudevī and Indrāyaṇī (D. Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 167). This inscription treats Viṣṇudevī and Indrāyaṇī as deities of equal rank. Over time, however, Viṣṇudevī became the principal focus of worship, leading to the site being known as the ViṣṇudevīTemple. A comparable transformation is observed in Nuwakot, where the medieval temple of GaṇḍakīBhairava evolved into the Bhairavī Temple during the Śāha period, as Bhairavī(Viṣṇudevī)gained prominence (D. Vajrācārya & T. Śreṣṭha VS 2037, p. 3).Among themukhākṛtis enshrined at Macchegāũ, the central image representsViṣṇudevī, the principalAjimā(clan goddess). TheDeśāracommunity of Macchegāũ has long maintained a close ritual association with this goddess. Members of this community conduct the dailypūjāand eveningāration a rotational basis and also play leading roles in the annualjātrā(festival procession). Other local groups participate mainly in ancillary duties such as musical performance (bādyavādana) and devotional singing.On the 9th of bright fortnight of Mārga, the facial feature (mukhākṛti) of Viṣṇudevī is ceremonially placed on akhaṭa(portable palanquin) and taken outside the temple. The images of the accompanying deities are arranged on either side, whileBhairava’sface is affixed atop achyāṅvessel filled with liquor, which is carried along with thekhaṭato thepīṭhaon the morning of tenth day. At thepīṭha, these deities are worshipped through ritual offerings andbali-pūjāthroughout the night. Meanwhile, themukhākṛtis of another Viṣṇudevī from Satuṅgala (SAT0010) are placed on thepīṭhathe night before, and hence thekhaṭaof Macchegāũ’s Viṣṇudevī remains positioned outside thepīṭhaduring the ritual. Around midday, the palanquin is lifted and joyfully carried back to the village amid music and celebration.On the  nineth day, when the deity’s face is mounted on thekhaṭa, the Dāphā Bhajana Group of Macchegāũ performs devotional songs before the temple—a practice also observed during Daśaĩ. Near this temple stands a small brickdeval(MCG0020-005) dedicated to Gaṇeśa, the Sthānagaṇeśa of theLāchhiquarter. This deity receives special worship during domestic rituals and life-cycle ceremonies. The custom of invoking Gaṇeśa first during Cathāḥ and other major festivals continues to be observed today (one of theguṭhīmembers of theDeśāra Guṭhī, male, age 53).
description_ne: द्यःछेँमा शाक्त मूर्तिहरू राखिने पराम्परा भएकोमा अपवादका रूपमा यहाँ भने द्यःछेँमै गाभेर तीन तले मन्दिर पनि उठाइएको छ ।मच्छेगाउँ सानो आकारको नेवारबस्ती हो । नेवार बस्तीमा अनिवार्य स्थापना हुने क्षेत्रपाल अर्थात् शाक्त देवीमध्ये यहाँ विष्णुदेवी छन् । स्वरूपमा तीनतले मन्दिर भए तापनि यो वास्तवमा द्यःछेँ हो । बस्ती बाहिरको अमूर्त पीठलाई प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने मूर्त प्रतिमा बस्तीभित्र द्यःछेँको पहिलो तलामा स्थापना भएको हुन्छ । यो प्राय सबै नेवारबस्तीको समान (common) परम्परा हो । यहाँ पनि यही दर्शन अनुरूप भूमि तलामा नभई पहिलो तलामा देवीको मूर्त मुखाकृति छ । विष्णुदेवीका साथमा शाक्त गणका अन्य मुखाकृति भैरव, गणेश, चामुण्डा (कालिका), माहेश्वरी इत्यादि छन् । विसं २०२० को दशकमा यहाँ भएका सक्कल मुखाकृतिहरू चोरिए पश्चात् पुनर्स्थापित नक्कलप्रति हुन् । चोर्न असफल गणेशको मुखाकृतिमात्र पुरानो प्रति हो । यी मुखाकृति राखिएको संरचना विगत द्यःछेँ थियो । आयताकार पूर्व-पश्चिम लम्बिएको दुईतले द्यःछेँमा थप दुई तहको पुर (फूचा) उठाउँदा यो तीन तले पेगोडा मन्दिरका रूपमा उठान भएको देखिन्छ । यसको मोहोडामा दुई सिंह स्थापित छन् जुन नेसं ७९० (सन् १७२०) का हुन् । दुई सिंहमाझ बुट्टेदार ढोका हालिएको छ जसमाथि तोरण चढाइएको छ । यस तोरण विसं २०५० को दशकमा चोरी भए पश्चात् पुनर्स्थापित नक्कल प्रति हो । ढोकाका दायाँ-बायाँ दुई ध्वज खडा छन् । मन्दिरका तीनै तला विगत झिंगटीले छाइएको थियो । पछिल्लो महाभूकम्प पश्चात्‌को पुनर्निर्माणमा सबै तहाका छाना तामाले मोडिएका छन् ।यस मन्दिर/द्यःछेँको निर्माणमिति निश्चित गर्न सकिने अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । यहाँ प्राप्त सर्वप्राचीन अभिलेख नेसं ७९० (सन् १६७०) को हो । यस अभिलेखमा विष्णुदेवी र इन्द्रायणीको नाममा सिंह प्रतिमा चढाइएको कुरा छ (D. Vajracārya VS 2056, p. 167) । यहाँ प्राप्त सर्वप्राचीन यस अभिलेखमा विष्णुदेवी र इन्द्रायणीलाई समान स्तरमा पुकारिएको छ । कालान्तरमा यहाँ विष्णुदेवी प्रमुख रूपमा लिई विष्णुदेवी मन्दिर कहलिन पुगेको देखिन्छ । नुवाकोटमा पनि मध्यकालमा गण्डकी भैरवका रूपमा प्रसिद्ध मन्दिर शाहकालमा भैरवी (विष्णुदेवी) प्रमुख बनी ‘भैरवी मन्दिर’मा परिणत हुन पुगेको छ (D. Vajracārya & T. Śreṣṭha VS 2037, p. 3) । यहाँ भएका मुखाकृतिमध्ये मध्य भागमा राखिएको मुखाकृति विष्णुदेवी अर्थात् मुख्य अजिमाका रूपमा पुजिदै आएको छ । मच्छेगाउँका देसार समुदायको यस विष्णुदेवीसँग विशेष सम्बन्ध रही आएको छ । देसार समुदायबाटै पालैपालो यहाँ नित्यपूजा र बेलुकी आरती हुने गरेको छ । जात्रामा पनि प्रमुख भूमिकामा यही समुदायका मानिसहरू रहन्छन् । बाद्यवादन र भजनकीर्तन जस्ता अतिरिक्त जिम्मेवारीमा मात्र अन्य समुदायको सहभागिता रही आएको छ । यहाँ भएका मुखाकृतिलाई मंसिर शुक्ल नवमीका दिन बाहिर निकाली खटमा राखिन्छ । यिनका अलावा अन्य देवगणका मुखाकृति पनि दायाँ-बायाँ राखिन्छन् । भैरवको मुखाकृति भने थ्वक्वं अर्थात् छ्याङ्गको घ्याम्पोमाथि टाँसिन्छ र उक्त घ्याम्पो पनि खटसँगै जात्रा गरी दशमीको विहानी पीठमा लगिन्छ । अन्य मातृकाका जात्रामा पीठमा लगिएका मुखाकृतिलाई रातभर पीठको अमूर्त ढुङ्गामाथि राखी बलिपूजा सहितको यज्ञ गरिन्छ । बःखुमण्डपस्थित पीठमा सतुङ्गलबाट खटमा राखी ल्याइएका अर्को बिष्णुदेवीका मुखाकृतिहरू (SAT0010) अघिल्लो रातमै पीठमाथि राखी सकेको हुन्छ । यसर्थ मच्छेगाउँस्थित विष्णुदेवीको मुखाकृति भएको खट पीठकोक वाहिरै राखी पूजा गरिन्छ । मध्यान्हको समय खट उठाई बस्ती फर्काई हर्षोल्हास गर्ने थिति छ । नवमीको दिन मुखाकृति खटमा राखिँदा मन्दिरको अग्र भागमा मच्छेगाँउको दाफा भजन समुहले भजन गाउँने थित छ । त्यसैगरी दशैंमा पनि यहाँ भजन हुने गर्दछ । यस मन्दिर नजिकै गणेशको देवल (MCG0020-005) छ । उक्त गणेश लाछि टोलवासीको स्थानगणेश भएकाले संस्कारजन्य कार्यमा यो गणेशलाई विशेष पूजा गर्ने थिति छ । चथाः एवं अन्य विशेष पर्वमा पनि गणेशलाई सुरुमा पुज्ने थिति चल्दै आएको छ (one of the guṭhī members of the Deśāra Guṭhī, male, age 53) ।

historical_events.event_description: A pair of stone lion sculptures (siṃha-pratimā) was installed in the name of Viṣṇudevī and Indrāyaṇī. An inscription bearing the donors’ names and further details of this installation is preserved together with the lions (MCG0020_I_002).
Under the leadership ofduvāra(guard?) Saterāma (Satyarāma?) and his wife Vimmarā, residents of Macchegāũ, two lion images were consecrated in the name of Viṣṇudevī and Indrāyaṇī.

An unidentified donor from Macchegāuṅ performed some act of dedication in the name of Viṣṇudevī. Since the lower portion of the inscription is worn away, the precise nature of this act is unclear. Dhanavajra (VS 2056, p. 425) records the full text, although with numerous inaccuracies. Judging from that corrupted reading, it seems that amukha(possibly an icon or mask) of Viṣṇudevī was established and certain ritual elements (pusidhāma,gatutadhika?) were affixed. The act was carried out by theGopālī(also calledGopārikaorGwālā) group, including Dhanarāma Gopārika of Macchegāuṅ. Although theGopālīcommunity has long inhabited areas such as Kīrtipura, Macchegāũ, Cobhāra, and Thānakoṭa, there are very few inscriptions attesting to their historical presence; therefore, this record is of particular importance.

Thedāphā khalaḥ(musical association) of Nhutanikvātha (Macchegāũ) offered a bell (ghaṇṭa) in the name of Viṣṇudevī. This act was led by Manahora Thārra and Yatimanisiṃha Tharrā. In addition, several men and women together presented silver coins as offerings to Viṣṇudevī.
Sūryanārāyaṇadeva and Jagatanārāyaṇadeva, sons of the late Jītanārāyaṇadeva Mānandhara, paved the forecourt of the Viṣṇudevī temple with a black stone slab.
The family of Rāmakṛṣṇa Lavata, residents of Macchegāũ, dedicated onepatāḥ(ceremonial banner) in the name of Viṣṇudevī.
The family of Kālu Bahādura Deśāra, inhabitants of Macchegāũ, offered oneghaṇṭa(bell) in the name of Viṣṇudevī.
In 2019 CE (VS 2076), the same family of Kālu Bahādura Deśāra, who had previously donated a bell, again dedicated onepatāḥin the name of Viṣṇudevī.
